profile.headline: Infrastructure · Distributed Systems · Production Engineering
profile.summary:
I'm the person who gets called when systems are broken in ways that cross boundaries—when the root cause is technical but tangled in organizational dynamics, when reliability has eroded and no one's sure why, when something critical needs to exist and no one knows how to start.

I've spent 20+ years in distributed systems, production engineering, and backend architecture. I've turned around failing services, rebuilt observability from scratch, and shaped engineering cultures around ownership and clarity. My work happens at the intersection of code, communication, and coordination—I make complexity tractable so teams can move.

I recently took a sabbatical to return to first principles. I built a production-grade Kubernetes cluster from bare metal—netboot provisioning, Ceph storage, Cilium networking, full observability stack—as a platform for exploring how AI can reason about infrastructure and compress the investigative cycle.

I'm excited about starting a new role working on embedded software this year (2026), a new mountain for me to climb. Lots of new things for me to learn.

positions.title: Senior Staff Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description: Starting a new role with Mainspring Energy on March 30, 2026 - super excited!

positions.title: Professional development
positions.description:
My measure of effective AI-augmented engineering isn't "I compressed two weeks into twelve hours."

It's "I eliminated a class of failures" or "I established invariants that hold under stress, growth, and turnover." Speed is a byproduct. The real leverage is judgment - knowing which layer is lying, which question to ask next, and what "done" looks like for a system that has to survive contact with reality.

I've been pressure-testing this belief by building an enterprise-grade Kubernetes cluster at home: netboot provisioning, Ansible automation, distributed storage on Ceph, Cilium for networking and BGP routing, automated DNS, TLS everywhere with short-lived certificates via Step CA, and full observability through Grafana, Loki, Tempo, and Mimir.

I call it the Goddess Cluster - every node named after a goddess from a different tradition. The cluster maintains full availability through any single node failure, and storage survives the loss of any two nodes without data loss.

It's a platform for exploring how AI can reason about infrastructure and the complex dynamics of distributed systems. When I find something interesting in a thread dump or on the network, I use LLMs to generate hypotheses and compress the investigative cycle. I'm researching how to surface relevant, high-signal telemetry to models and how to frame the incident-response loop as an agent-driving framework. Early days, but I love describing an anomaly to an LLM and collaboratively producing targeted eBPF probes to get real evidence about system behavior.

positions.title: Production Engineer
positions.description:
Returned to Meta in a staff-level IC capacity with a unique cross-org mandate: identify and unblock critical reliability and efficiency issues across the data warehouse compute stack. Contributed to scheduler redesigns, cross-team coordination, and hard-to-track workload failures—especially during the company-wide “year of efficiency” initiative.

Key Contributions:

• Served under the head of Data Infra Compute, with a broad investigative role spanning Presto, Spark, Warehouse Foundation, and DataOps.

• Influenced planning and scope for a major scheduler redesign effort, advocating for practical instrumentation, better prioritization signals, and lightweight prototypes.

• Investigated Spark workloads skirting prioritization, surfaced non-compliant patterns, and helped bring them into alignment.

• Acted as a technical bridge between DataOps and Compute/Infra teams to reconnect roadmap and prioritization efforts for shared reliability goals.

• Diagnosed a warehouse-wide pipeline degradation caused by SKU drift in Presto scheduling—fix shaved hours off critical data landing time each day.

• Mentored other production engineers, helping revive agility and confidence across teams through targeted coaching and systems thinking.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Returned to Mode briefly to support the backend team during a period of performance degradation and architectural transition. Contributed targeted improvements, mentored engineers, and laid groundwork for long-term schema scalability.

Key Impacts:

• Identified architectural performance issues across Java and Go services by analyzing CPU traces and heap dumps from crashing production instances.

• Reduced memory footprint of schema processing services by 75%, improving uptime and eliminating redundant schema queries to customer databases.

• Mentored backend engineers on profiling and performance diagnosis techniques, using live case studies from production.

• Advocated for and initiated architectural discussions around streaming-based schema indexing to support large-scale datasets.

• Kicked off planning for a third-party database driver quality certification program to ensure reliability and compatibility across customer integrations.

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description:
Launched an early-stage venture exploring data-driven machine learning products in commercial real estate. Led technical strategy, data acquisition, and feature engineering efforts for an MVP viability model, while building operational structure and alignment in a volatile founding environment.

Key Contributions:

    • Built a custom data scraper to aggregate and normalize commercial property listings from multiple sources into structured training data (including data cleaning, enrichment, and storage).

    • Led technical design and planning for an ML pipeline to support a regression model for tenant viability prediction.

    • Established MVP-focused planning cadence, and facilitated engineering prioritization and alignment among cofounders.

    • Advised and supported a newly trained data scientist (first-time collaborator) on feature development and tradeoffs.

Outcome:
Wound down operations due to early-stage cofounder misalignment and external market instability during COVID-19 onset.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Hired into a backend leadership role during a pivotal stage in the company’s growth. Took initiative across boundaries—refactoring core systems, improving cross-team reliability, and helping customer success reduce escalations through backend visibility and self-service tooling. Shaped technical direction and roadmap priorities through influence and clarity of purpose.

Key Impacts:

    • Took ownership of database driver performance and reliability, reducing customer query issues and improving team-wide service stability.

    • Led a major refactor of the query service, modularizing instrumentation, error handling, and configuration to improve reliability and surface top errors faster.

    • Worked directly with major customers to troubleshoot database connectivity issues—identified root causes in client-side infrastructure and contributed fixes to their Presto gateway proxy.

    • Collaborated with prospective clients during the sales cycle to understand their needs and build key features that helped close new contracts.

    • Initiated structured collaboration between backend engineering and customer success—established weekly triage cycles, uncovered key bugs, built shared tools, and reduced escalations by 90%.

    • Mentored three engineers (junior and senior), assigning ownership and helping grow confidence and autonomy.

    • Launched recurring incident reviews and response processes, building reliability culture across backend teams.

    • Formed and advocated for a cross-functional senior IC working group (with executive buy-in) to address long-standing performance, architecture, and ownership gaps.

positions.title: Production Engineer
positions.description:
Returned to Facebook and joined the Data Infrastructure team, focused on stabilizing batch compute systems (Hive on Corona, Presto, Spark) during a period of high operational friction. Took on an engineering leadership role guiding technical direction, reliability strategy, and cross-team coordination across critical infrastructure components.

Key Impacts:

    • Led the cultural and technical shift toward user-centered reliability by reconciling internal SLIs with real-world developer pain—long queue times, failed retries, and undiagnosed job delays.

    • Defined and tracked new metrics for final failure states, labeling root causes through extensive query and log parsing; influenced prioritization and roadmap adjustments across multiple teams.

    • Investigated performance variability and fragility in dataswarm workflows, revealing critical inefficiencies in job retries, query configurations, and dependency resolution logic.

    • Co-designed a dependency analysis tool to map and estimate downstream workloads impacted by errors to critical, foundational fact tables, enabling fast, cost-aware recovery orchestration.

    • Advised and supported adoption of best practices in configuration, scheduling pools, and pipeline standardization across orgs.

Engineering Leadership:

    • Worked with directors to shape reliability-focused technical direction across compute teams, including Spark, Hive, and Presto, aligning priorities and roadmap commitments.

    • Mentored engineers and promoted systems-level thinking around reliability, observability, and operational feedback loops.

    • Became a go-to source for insight and triage around batch performance and failure modes.

positions.title: Chief Architect
positions.description:
Joined during a post-acquisition unification effort to help define architecture and engineering practices for a new global security services division. Despite personal upheaval during this time, contributed to core strategy discussions, team formation, and early infrastructure scaffolding that shaped the organization’s future direction.

Key Impacts:

    • Led initial architecture work to consolidate and align services from multiple acquired entities into a cohesive security platform strategy.

    • Oversaw early design and development of GTIP (Global Threat Intelligence Platform), including technical direction and system goals for ingest, analysis, and enrichment workflows.

    • Bootstrapped a new SRE team and introduced early infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD guardrails, and release hygiene practices to reduce operational risk.

    • Mentored engineers on improving reliability and development velocity through automated testing, linting, and deployment standards.

positions.title: Senior Technical Consultant
positions.description:
Brought in to lead the migration of an application firewall and intrusion detection system for a U.S. federal agency. Delivered a clean transition from legacy tooling to AWS-native network access controls through custom-built automation and reverse engineering, all under strict government operational constraints.

Key Impacts:

    • Reverse-engineered Trend Micro’s configuration and audit data structures to design a migration tool translating legacy firewall rules into AWS-native equivalents (e.g. security groups, NACLs).

    • Automated the full configuration export, transformation, and rehydration process to eliminate manual toil and reduce migration risk.

    • Addressed deep technical debt, including unoptimized database schema (e.g. never-vacuumed audit logs), improving performance of internal systems.

    • Navigated restricted time windows, RDP-only access, and policy overhead to complete all deliverables on schedule.

    • Identified forward-looking architecture improvements, though these were deferred due to institutional limits.

positions.title: Database Performance Engineer / Production Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on Facebook’s data compute infrastructure powering all batch workloads via Hive on Corona (a fork of MapReduce), Presto, and HDFS. Helped steer the system through a major inflection point as storage efficiencies shifted the primary bottleneck to compute capacity. Contributed to both deep technical troubleshooting and cross-org operational reform to improve system reliability, resource efficiency, and performance.

Key Impacts:

    • Standardized job prioritization and slot allocation across internal orgs by interviewing engineers, analyzing workloads, and defining a unified set of scheduling pools, replacing a fragmented namespace-specific model.

    • Developed “Hiveswatter,” a mechanism to short-circuit known failing recurring Hive jobs early in execution, reclaiming valuable compute slots.

    • Diagnosed a critical scheduler bottleneck in Corona’s jobtracker caused by serialized task assignment with slow network calls—pinpointed the codepath and proposed fixes adopted by engineering leadership.

    • Resolved cluster-wide OOM crashes during cross-region replication by designing a workaround using an LD_PRELOAD-based connect syscall interceptor to dynamically adjust TCP socket buffer sizes based on destination subnet.

    • Collaborated with data infrastructure and storage teams during system-wide hardening to handle rising demand across Messenger, Ads, and other internal platforms.

    • Improved system resilience by triaging query scheduler behavior, eliminating runaway compute workloads, and pushing for consistent failure triage practices.

positions.title: Production Engineer / Production Engineering Manager
positions.description:
Joined during a period of systemic instability and team dysfunction on the HBase infrastructure team, which supported Messenger, internal monitoring systems, and search indexing. Promoted mid-year into a formal management role to help stabilize both the systems and the team. Focused on enabling strong but under-supported engineers to succeed, restoring operational health, and rebuilding trust across orgs under intense pressure.

Key Impacts:

    • Diagnosed and mitigated write-path latency issues across HBase and HDFS that were causing repeated crashes and outages in Messenger.

    • Facilitated effort to stabilize schema design and replication strategies, including live migrations of active clusters under load and redesign of backup/restore systems.

    • Advocated for halting feature development and prioritizing cross-functional reliability work—helping realign efforts across PE, SWE, and partner teams.

    • Brought focus and follow-through to a fractured team, enabling engineers to reclaim ownership of critical remediations and performance work.

    • Collaborated in cross-org crisis response planning and execution during hardware failures and data migration events.

    • Authored and shared weekly internal reports to keep stakeholders and leadership aligned on system health, risks, and progress.

People & Team Leadership:

    • Promoted with a “Redefines Expectations” rating in recognition of impact.

    • Managed hiring and mentoring for multiple team members who went on to excel.

    • Played a key role in unlocking peers: diagnosing blockers, modeling initiative, and seeding confidence through relationship-building and emotional intelligence.

    • Regularly took on “translator” roles between engineers and stakeholders to surface what mattered and get it unblocked.

Recognition:

    Honored with a public award for crisis leadership—recognized internally as a calm and catalytic force during high-severity operational events.

positions.title: Network Appliance Engineer
positions.description:
•	Architected new centralized management and change control system using Puppet, nginx, memcached, passenger, and ucarp.  Any changes to the system must be pushed via git, as updates to the Puppet masters are driven by post-receive hooks.
•	Refreshed internal yum repositories and built a process to automate RPM building for multiple target platforms in parallel using Fedora’s mock build utility.  This eased the transition from CentOS 5 to CentOS 6 by ensuring consistent package availability and versioning, and it also helps guarantee the integrity of the RPMs and their underlying dependencies to promote consistent behavior in production machines.
•	Developed a Puppet module for managing rsyslog deployments, including logic to dynamically tune the message queue sizes and number of worker threads based on available memory and processor cores on the target machine.
•	Created first ever integrated appliance platform combining the ActiveGuard Appliance with a partner’s solution to provide a hybrid log collector / forwarder + intrusion prevention system leveraging BotHunter at its core.  IDS monitoring work is distributed across multiple cores to improve overall monitoring throughput, and data copying from kernel space to user space is minimized as much as possible.  
•	Conducted bi-weekly Systems Engineering training for the Systems team, covering Puppet, “DevOps” related topics, and the overall architecture of our service offering so they can support it to the best of their ability.
•	Continued to own and promote the security training program in the SOC; collaborating with SOC management to ensure our analysts are well informed and on the cutting edge of the industry.

positions.title: Information Security Engineering Manager
positions.description:
•	Engaged in continuous process improvement and quality control to strengthen all phases of service delivery – specifically, developed a prioritized work queue for the engineers to streamline escalated event resolution.
•	Supported the Service Delivery Management team by organizing and streamlining setup process, kick-off meetings, project planning, tuning, normalization, troubleshooting and resource assignment to support new and existing clients.
•	Functioned in a technical QA oversight capacity to support the SOC on matters pertaining to process quality and delivery of Solutionary’s service offerings.
•	Worked with Systems and Development to onboard customers and complete baseline settings and normalization phases for ActiveGuard processing.
•	Drove process and toolset improvement for the front-end Portal by functioning as the operations sponsor for any proposed changes to the Portal.  Ensured changes promoting consistency, efficiency, and ease of use were prioritized according to need and potential ROI.
•	Collaborated with SOC Manager to improve interdepartmental coordination and continued to foster growth and development in the SOC through the engineer support corps.
•	Worked with the EVP of Operations and the CTO to create the Network Appliance Engineer position to promote the feature set we need for the ActiveGuard Appliance platform to fulfill our roadmap for the next few years.

positions.title: SOC Manager
positions.description:
•	Scheduled, oversaw, and directed SOC personnel administration activities including hiring, training, job assignment, performance evaluation, career pathing, compensation review, counseling, coaching and terminations for Omaha and Pittsburgh locations.
•	Coached and oversaw the SOC in operational activities to ensure compliance with customer contracts and Service Level Agreements, accurate and timely client deliverables, achievement of departmental goals, objectives, and budget.
•	Designed and implemented new processes and tools to support near real-time quantitative and qualitative performance trending and analysis for the SOC, leveraging custom SQL and Oracle analytic functions.  In turn, this data provided the majority of input into performance reviews, capacity planning, and revisions to training.
•	Created new, feedback driven new hire training curriculum and internal certification track for information security analysts.  Data from the previous quarter drives the content and focus of specific security modules, and feedback from previous training classes is integrated to continuously improve the quality of the program.
•	Developed and mentored an engineering support corps within the department to foster career pathing and to reduce escalations outside of the department and the overall turnaround time for client requests.

positions.title: Systems Engineer
positions.description:
Served in variety of roles from direct implementation to project technical lead to architect.
•	Designed and implemented an OpenVPN-based distributed appliance network with over 400 nodes around the world to support service delivery platform and reduced turn-up time by a factor of 15.
•	Deployed service polling and SNMP-based monitoring and alerting systems such as OpenNMS and increased service uptime in support of 99.999% uptime goals.
•	Implemented BGP-based bogon filtering in border gateway routers.
•	Engineered route verification solution integrating Quagga BGP, SQLite, and perl for in-house scanning system to prevent scanning non-routeable addresses and avoid ICMP floods. 
•	Automated CentOS Linux system provisioning via PXE boot and kickstart.
•	Reduced datacenter power and space requirements by converting existing physical systems to Xen and VMWare based virtual machines.
•	Maintained JBoss application server environment and worked alongside development staff to tune the platform to meet the needs of the application.
•	Tuned PostgreSQL database clusters for maximum throughput and performance on high transaction workload.
•	Ported ODBC-related Perl scripts and dependencies from legacy platforms to new, template based 64 bit production servers.
•	Established internal CentOS RPM mirror and created/maintained internal Yum repository to centralize patch management.

positions.title: Security Specialist
positions.description:
•	Monitored network logs and reviewed packet captures to detect potential security concerns on behalf of customers.
•	Automated repetitive technical processes via scripting with bash, ruby, and perl.
•	Conducted volunteer classes on improving Linux command line proficiency.

experience.title: Senior Staff Embedded Software Engineer
experience.description: Starting a new role with Mainspring Energy on March 30, 2026 - super excited!

experience.title: Professional development
experience.description:
My measure of effective AI-augmented engineering isn't "I compressed two weeks into twelve hours."

It's "I eliminated a class of failures" or "I established invariants that hold under stress, growth, and turnover." Speed is a byproduct. The real leverage is judgment - knowing which layer is lying, which question to ask next, and what "done" looks like for a system that has to survive contact with reality.

I've been pressure-testing this belief by building an enterprise-grade Kubernetes cluster at home: netboot provisioning, Ansible automation, distributed storage on Ceph, Cilium for networking and BGP routing, automated DNS, TLS everywhere with short-lived certificates via Step CA, and full observability through Grafana, Loki, Tempo, and Mimir.

I call it the Goddess Cluster - every node named after a goddess from a different tradition. The cluster maintains full availability through any single node failure, and storage survives the loss of any two nodes without data loss.

It's a platform for exploring how AI can reason about infrastructure and the complex dynamics of distributed systems. When I find something interesting in a thread dump or on the network, I use LLMs to generate hypotheses and compress the investigative cycle. I'm researching how to surface relevant, high-signal telemetry to models and how to frame the incident-response loop as an agent-driving framework. Early days, but I love describing an anomaly to an LLM and collaboratively producing targeted eBPF probes to get real evidence about system behavior.

positions.title: Database Performance Engineer / Production Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on Facebook’s data compute infrastructure powering all batch workloads via Hive on Corona (a fork of MapReduce), Presto, and HDFS. Key Impacts:

    • Standardized job prioritization and slot allocation across internal orgs by interviewing engineers, analyzing workloads, and defining a unified set of scheduling pools, replacing a fragmented namespace-specific model.

    • Developed “Hiveswatter,” a mechanism to short-circuit known failing recurring Hive jobs early in execution, reclaiming valuable compute slots.

    • Diagnosed a critical scheduler bottleneck in Corona’s jobtracker caused by serialized task assignment with slow network calls—pinpointed the codepath and proposed fixes adopted by engineering leadership.

    • Resolved cluster-wide OOM crashes during cross-region replication by designing a workaround using an LD_PRELOAD-based connect syscall interceptor to dynamically adjust TCP socket buffer sizes based on destination subnet.

    • Collaborated with data infrastructure and storage teams during system-wide hardening to handle rising demand across Messenger, Ads, and other internal platforms.

    • Improved system resilience by triaging query scheduler behavior, eliminating runaway compute workloads, and pushing for consistent failure triage practices.

positions.title: Network Appliance Engineer
positions.description:
•	Architected new centralized management and change control system using Puppet, nginx, memcached, passenger, and ucarp.  Any changes to the system must be pushed via git, as updates to the Puppet masters are driven by post-receive hooks.
•	Refreshed internal yum repositories and built a process to automate RPM building for multiple target platforms in parallel using Fedora’s mock build utility.  This eased the transition from CentOS 5 to CentOS 6 by ensuring consistent package availability and versioning, and it also helps guarantee the integrity of the RPMs and their underlying dependencies to promote consistent behavior in production machines.
•	Developed a Puppet module for managing rsyslog deployments, including logic to dynamically tune the message queue sizes and number of worker threads based on available memory and processor cores on the target machine.
•	Created first ever integrated appliance platform combining the ActiveGuard Appliance with a partner’s solution to provide a hybrid log collector / forwarder + intrusion prevention system leveraging BotHunter at its core.  IDS monitoring work is distributed across multiple cores to improve overall monitoring throughput, and data copying from kernel space to user space is minimized as much as possible.  
•	Conducted bi-weekly Systems Engineering training for the Systems team, covering Puppet, “DevOps” related topics, and the overall architecture of our service offering so they can support it to the best of their ability.
•	Continued to own and promote the security training program in the SOC; collaborating with SOC management to ensure our analysts are well informed and on the cutting edge of the industry.
